mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within the last month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in real GDP by more than 1% over the last quarter signals a weakening economy, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 declines and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 2% over the last two months signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports higher corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts by more than 5% over the last two months signals a strengthening demand side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased construction activity supports higher economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4.5% and the consumer price index increases by more than 0.5% in the last month, it indicates an inflationary environment with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns are eroded.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary environment with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL on negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 over the last month and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.3%, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending is expected to increase.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of increasing PAYEMS and decreasing UNRATE on positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A steady increase in real GDP by more than 0.5% over the last quarter, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.2% in the last month, signals a robust economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases > 0.5% in 1 quarter and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of increasing GDPC1 and decreasing UNRATE on positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
